clue.text: Establishment to make cut of nine hands

parts.note: to dock a tail or a wage is to cut it short
a hand is four inches, so nine of them make thirty-six inches, which is a yard

explanation.surface: A firm sets out to trim the pay of nine of its labourers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' looks like workers, but it is the horse-measuring unit of four inches. 'Establishment' is in the naval sense: a shipbuilding and repair base.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval dockyard is a shore establishment where ships are built and repaired.

clue.text: Round and jolly in wet surroundings he had tea poured on his nose

definitions.text: he had tea poured on his nose

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the word for soaking

parts.note: to douse is to wet thoroughly, here forming the surroundings
the letter O is round
a jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: A plump, cheerful man in the rain has tea poured over his face.
explanation.walkthrough: At the Mad Hatter's tea party in Alice in Wonderland, the Hatter pours a little hot tea on the sleepy rodent's nose.
explanation.definitionFit: In Carroll's tea party scene the drowsy rodent guest is woken by tea poured on its nose.

clue.text: Escorts engaged at Worcester

explanation.surface: Gallant companions fought at the Battle of Worcester.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallant gentlemen who escort ladies are cavaliers; the Royalists who fought Cromwell at Worcester in 1651 were called Cavaliers.

clue.text: Why altaltissimo — the highest summit — includes this place

indicators.note: the letter string of the opening words includes, holds within it, the place name

explanation.surface: A musical marking for the very top notes is likened to the loftiest peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The highest summit' is a hint: the 1945 Yalta Conference was a summit of Churchill, Roosevelt and Stalin.
explanation.definitionFit: Yalta is a Crimean resort town, the location of the 1945 summit.

clue.text: Very little breadth in the show, but it produces income

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a revue is a theatrical show of sketches and songs
an en is a printer's unit, half an em, a very small width

explanation.surface: A thin show still turns a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is the money an organisation takes in, its income.

clue.text: Shift to second home

parts.note: a hovel is a humble, squalid home

explanation.surface: Someone moves house to a second residence.
explanation.definitionFit: To shovel is to move earth or snow in bulk, so it means to shift.

clue.text: Intuitive feeling to support Richard III, say

parts.note: a hunch is a gut feeling
to back is to support

explanation.surface: Someone has a feeling they should back King Richard III.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Richard III is portrayed with a deformed back.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradition and Shakespeare depict Richard III with a curved spine, an example of such a person.

clue.text: Come out with a means of communication

explanation.surface: Someone speaks up using a way of communicating.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice an opinion is to utter it; the human speaking faculty is a means of communication.

clue.text: Scope for small rise in deposit

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to lay is to deposit, as a bird lays eggs

indicators.note: in a down clue, rise means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: There is room for a slight increase in a payment held as security.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns WEE into EEW, which sits inside LAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is room to manoeuvre, freedom or latitude.

clue.text: "And one by one back in the — lays" (Fitzgerald)

definitions.text: "And one by one back in the — lays" (Fitzgerald)

parts.words: "And one by one back in the — lays" (Fitzgerald)
parts.note: the solver fills the gap in a line from FitzGerald's Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam, where the Master of the Show puts his pieces away in a cupboard

explanation.surface: A line from Edward FitzGerald's Rubaiyat with one word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The verse: 'Hither and thither moves, and checks, and slays, / And one by one back in the — lays.' The missing word is a small private cupboard or room.
explanation.definitionFit: The word missing from FitzGerald's verse is a small storage cupboard.

clue.text: Composer to tease

explanation.surface: A composer sets out to make fun of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Ravel was the French composer of Boléro; to ravel is to tangle or untangle threads, as wool is teased.

clue.text: Silvia's suitor names the day

explanation.surface: A young man courting Silvia finally fixes the wedding date.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Two Gentlemen of Verona the hero wooing Silvia bears this name, and the same name labels the saint's day of 14 February.

clue.text: Pilots in a mess catering for artists

indicators.note: a mess is a muddle, so the letters of the words before it are jumbled up

explanation.surface: Airmen in their officers' mess are cooking for painters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mess' suggests the airmen's dining room, but 'in a mess' is the anagram signal: PILOTS IN A shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Paints ground in linseed are the classic supplies an easel painter buys, so they cater for artists.

clue.text: He's involved with any carnivore

indicators.note: involved means tangled together, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: He's is read as the word he

explanation.surface: A man has some connection with any meat-eater.
explanation.definitionFit: The striped and spotted scavengers of African plains are flesh-eating mammals.

clue.text: Jack's high point

parts.note: read Jack as the second half of the name for a man who climbs and repairs church spires, and the high point is where he works

explanation.surface: Someone called Jack reaches the peak of his career.
explanation.definitionFit: A church spire is a tall structure, the workplace that gives the steeple-climbing workman his name.

clue.text: Trio of equal value to William and Mary for example

explanation.surface: Three things are worth the same to the joint monarchs William and Mary.
explanation.walkthrough: In card games a pair royal is three cards of the same rank. William III and Mary II reigned jointly, a royal couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Three cards of equal rank form a pair royal in old card games; William and Mary, joint monarchs, were literally a royal couple.

clue.text: Type of square design for roofing

parts.note: a T-square is a drawing instrument, so the letter T names that type
to hatch a plot is to design it

explanation.surface: A particular square pattern is chosen for covering a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Straw or reed laid as a roof covering is the traditional cottage roofing material.

clue.text: Direction given by a horologist?

parts.note: a horologist is a clockmaker, so his advice is wise about timepieces, while the term also names a turning direction

explanation.surface: A clockmaker gives instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: The way the hands of a timepiece turn is the rotation direction named after them.

clue.text: Insults with a loud sort of snort

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

indicators.note: sort of signals a rearranged version of the word snort

explanation.surface: Someone gives offence with a noisy snort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges SNORT as RONTS. FF is strictly 'very loud' in music.
explanation.definitionFit: Affronts are open insults or slights.

clue.text: One receiving property like Leo for example

parts.note: as means like, in the same way
Leo is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Someone resembling a Leo is about to inherit an estate.
explanation.walkthrough: In legal English an assign is a person to whom property or a right is transferred, an assignee.
explanation.definitionFit: In law an assign is the transferee who takes over property or rights from another.

clue.text: Head worker nodding

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A chief employee is dozing off.
explanation.walkthrough: NUTANT is a botanical word for drooping or nodding, as a flower head does.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanists use this term for flower heads that droop or bow.

clue.text: Garden work for profit?

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether gardening pays.
explanation.definitionFit: Raking leaves off a lawn is a garden chore; a rake-off is a share of profits, often illicit.

clue.text: In a hurry to fire rifle

parts.note: someone who ran was moving in a hurry
to sack is to fire from a job

explanation.surface: Someone rushes to shoot a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rifle' and 'fire' suggest a gun, but rifle is the verb meaning to search and steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to ransack it, searching through it to steal.

clue.text: Come forward to raise output

explanation.surface: Workers are urged to come forward and increase production.
explanation.definitionFit: To step up is to volunteer by coming forward, and also to increase production.

clue.text: Head of the scruffy grey animal captured by Blake

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
scruffy means untidy, so the letters of grey are messed up

explanation.surface: A scruffy grey creature is caught by a man called Blake.
explanation.walkthrough: William Blake's poem opens 'Tyger Tyger, burning bright', using his old spelling of the beast.
explanation.definitionFit: Blake's poem captured the striped big cat in verse under this archaic spelling.

clue.text: Mountain feature could catch one out

explanation.surface: A mountain landmark might trap a climber.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, gully is a close fielding position where catches dismiss batsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A gully is a ravine cut into a mountainside; in cricket the fielder at gully may take a catch.

clue.text: Strange term taken from St Paul, for example

indicators.note: strange means odd or unusual, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd word is lifted from the writings of St Paul.
explanation.walkthrough: Acts 18 says Paul worked at his trade making shelters of cloth and skins, so he is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul the apostle earned his living by stitching canvas shelters, according to Acts.

clue.text: Queen over the Spanish so called

parts.note: Queen Mab is the fairy queen of Mercutio's speech in Romeo and Juliet
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A queen ruling Spain bears this title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so called' means a girl given this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name is what she is called.

clue.text: Two girls one excessively optimistic

parts.note: Polly is a girl's name
Anna is another girl's name

explanation.surface: Of two girls, one is far too hopeful.
explanation.walkthrough: The name comes from Eleanor H. Porter's 1913 novel whose heroine always finds something to be glad about.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of Porter's novel gave her name to anyone relentlessly cheerful and hopeful.

clue.text: Child I join in sort of dance

indicators.note: the letter joins in, entering the middle of the dance word

parts.note: a barn dance is a kind of country dance

explanation.surface: A child says she will take part in a kind of dance.
explanation.walkthrough: BAIRN is the Scottish and northern English word for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots speech uses this word for a youngster or baby.

clue.text: Bribe — give ring to lady being cut in half

parts.note: to pay is to give money
the letter O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: cutting a four-letter word in half leaves its first two letters

explanation.surface: Someone offers a lady a ring as she is sawn in two in a magic act.
explanation.walkthrough: PAYOLA is American slang for secret payments, especially to disc jockeys to play records.
explanation.definitionFit: Payola is an illicit payment made for favours, especially for airplay.

clue.text: Craft set out to collect pots

parts.note: craft means skill or expertise

indicators.note: out means awry, so the letters of set are rearranged

explanation.surface: A craftsman heads off to gather some pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: Skillets are frying pans or long-handled cooking vessels.
